title: WAYS TO SELL EXISTING CONSUMABLE PRODUCTS
content:
If the consumable product belongs to another company, you still need to decide what role you want in the sale and what happens when the customer needs more.

Common routes include network/direct selling, affiliate/referral marketing, reselling inventory, and dropshipping. The important difference is not just how the first order happens. It is whether repeat purchases remain connected to you and under what terms.

NETWORK / DIRECT SALES
Depending on the company, customers may remain associated with a particular seller or account, allowing qualifying repeat purchases to continue contributing to compensation. The exact structure, retail requirements, customer attribution, qualifications, and compensation rules must be verified from the current company materials.

AFFILIATE MARKETING
You refer the customer to a merchant. Some programs compensate only the attributed transaction. Others may have different rules. Do not assume a repeat purchase creates another commission unless the program explicitly says so.

RESELLING
You buy and resell inventory. A repeat customer can return to your business, but you remain responsible for stocking or obtaining product and serving the transaction.

DROPSHIPPING
You operate the sale while a supplier ships the product. Repeat orders can come through your storefront, but supplier reliability and customer experience remain important dependencies.

THE QUESTION TO CARRY FORWARD
When this customer runs out, what exactly has to happen for their next purchase to create income for my business?

WHY REPEAT ATTRIBUTION DESERVES SPECIAL ATTENTION

A seller can truthfully say "customers reorder this product" while still having a business where the seller receives nothing from later purchases. That is why the repeat mechanism needs to be investigated directly.

For every arrangement, ask:
Who processes the reorder?
Does the customer remain connected to my account, store, or referral?
For how long?
What can break that connection?
What conditions must I continue meeting?
Who controls the rules?

Those answers matter more than the generic fact that the product gets used up.
